content: The bifluoride ion, also known as the hydrogen (difluoride) ion, is represented as HF₂⁻. This centrosymmetric triatomic anion is characterized by the strongest known hydrogen bond, with an F−H bond length of 114 pm and a bond strength exceeding 155 kJ mol⁻¹. A molecular orbital diagram indicates that the atoms in this ion are held together by a three-center, four-electron bond. The term hydrogen (difluoride) is written as a single word because it refers to an anion. If written as hydrogen difluoride, it would imply an electrically neutral compound, HF₂, which does not exist. The bifluoride ion is also present in certain compounds, such as tetra-n-butylammonium fluoride. Additionally, the bifluoride ion plays a role in the unusually high auto-protolysis constant of liquid anhydrous hydrofluoric acid. This acid undergoes autodissociation in a manner similar to the self-ionization of water.
